# Quiet Sonar Playbook

## Hiding Strategy

When choosing where to hide my submarine, I will avoid positions 5-8 in early rounds, as this middle-to-upper range gets probed repeatedly by opponents. I'll rotate between lower positions (1-4) and higher positions (8-9) based on the patterns I observe in opponent firing.

When I see opponents consistently firing at a particular position across multiple rounds while claiming misses, those positions become safe to hide in—their pattern suggests they've already ruled them out.

When hiding in the final round, I will choose a position in the lower range (1-3) that hasn't been the focus of observed firing patterns, as opponents tend to concentrate fire in the middle ranges.

## Firing Strategy

When I fire at my target each round, I will start by probing middle positions (4-6) in early rounds to gather information about my target's likely location.

After observing opponent firing patterns across multiple rounds, I will shift my fire toward positions they haven't targeted, since this is where their submarines are likely to be.

In the final round, I can afford to fire at higher intensity positions since there's no recovery opportunity afterward. I'll commit to a guess based on accumulated pattern evidence rather than playing conservatively.

## Claiming Strategy

When I fire and receive the true result, I will always claim truthfully—hit or miss—matching exactly what the referee told me. Since all fires are public, false claims cannot be sustained and risk damaging my credibility. Credibility matters in a multiplayer game because opponents' behavior and information-sharing may be influenced by whether they trust me.

I have consistently scored 0 points or negative points across all episodes, primarily because I've missed many shots on my target Foxtrot. This suggests my firing strategy has not been effective at locating my target. In future games, I need to develop a more systematic approach to narrowing down opponent positions rather than choosing semi-randomly among middle positions.
